title: Gyanwati v. State of U.P.
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Kshitij Shailendra, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; EE to consider theft-assessment objection under Supply Code
headnote: A writ seeking a direction to decide an objection to a theft-based provisional assessment is disposed of on the licensee's statement that the Executive Engineer will consider the objection before the final assessment, with a direction that the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 procedure be strictly followed.
facts: Gyanwati was issued a notice of provisional assessment by the Electricity Department in a case of alleged theft of electricity. She filed an application dated 22 December 2023 objecting to that notice and then approached the Allahabad High Court in Writ-C No. 11825 of 2024, praying for a direction to respondent no. 2 to decide the objection. The Department appeared through counsel. The writ was listed before a Division Bench of Manoj Kumar Gupta and Kshitij Shailendra, JJ. on 10 April 2024.

holding_units.topic: provisional assessment — theft — objection before final order
holding_units.holding: On the licensee's statement that the Executive Engineer would consider the consumer's objection to a theft-based provisional assessment before passing the final assessment order, the writ was disposed of with a direction that the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 shall be strictly followed while considering the objection.

not_decided.point: Merits of the alleged theft and of the provisional assessment or objection
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the assessment or the objection; it recorded the Department's statement and directed Supply Code procedure.
